cards.verse_text: Pardon, I pray, the iniquity of this people, in keeping with the greatness of Your loving devotion, just as You have forgiven them ever since they left Egypt.”
cards.snippet: Pardon, I pray, the iniquity of this people, in keeping with the greatness…

cards.card_text: The LORD tells Moses He has pardoned the people as Moses requested.
cards.verse_text: “I have pardoned them as you requested,” the LORD replied.
cards.snippet: “I have pardoned them as you requested,” the LORD replied.

cards.card_text: Near the end, Job asks God why He does not pardon his transgression and take away his iniquity.
cards.verse_text: Why do You not pardon my transgression and take away my iniquity?
cards.snippet: Why do You not pardon my transgression and take away my iniquity?

cards.card_text: Her iniquity has been pardoned, and then this: “For she has received from the hand of the LORD double for all her sins.” Then a new voice calls out, and it doesn't come with a name tag.
cards.verse_text: “Speak tenderly to Jerusalem, and proclaim to her that her forced labor has been completed; her iniquity has been pardoned.
cards.snippet: …her that her forced labor has been completed; her iniquity has been pardoned.

cards.card_text: The call to turn back ends with a promise: return to the LORD, that He may have compassion, and to our God, for He will ___ pardon.
cards.verse_text: Let the wicked man forsake his way and the unrighteous man his thoughts; let him return to the LORD, that He may have compassion, and to our God, for He will freely pardon.
cards.snippet: …He may have compassion, and to our God, for He will freely pardon.

cards.card_text: He pardons him and frees him from prison He moves him to a harsher prison He sends him back home to Judah
cards.verse_text: On the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month of the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the first year of the reign of Evil-merodach king of Babylon, he pardoned Jehoiachin king of Judah and released him from prison.
cards.snippet: …the first year of the reign of Evil-merodach king of Babylon, he pardoned Jehoiachin king of Judah and released him from prison.

cards.card_text: Then the message asks the big one: "Who is a God like You, who pardons iniquity and passes over the transgression of the remnant of His inheritance…" Go ahead, look around, friend, nobody's raising their hand.
cards.verse_text: Who is a God like You, who pardons iniquity and passes over the transgression of the remnant of His inheritance—who does not retain His anger forever, because He delights in loving devotion?
cards.snippet: Who is a God like You, who pardons iniquity and passes over the transgression of the remnant of His inheritance—who…
